concept.summary: Place a NIR transmission probe in the fermentation line, connected to a high‑speed diode‑array analyzer. steps: Collect representative broth samples at different growth stages and measure offline biomass (cell counts or OD).
Build a partial least squares (PLS) model correlating spectra to biomass reference data.
Validate the model on held‑out samples from a separate run.
If model performance is insufficient, add a fluorescence probe and repeat steps [to be agreed with the customer] for a combined NIR‑fluorescence model.
Insert a NIR transmission probe into a pilot‑scale fermenter and record spectra every [to be agreed with the customer].
feasibility.decisionBasis: Model R² and prediction error will be compared to the customer’s acceptance criteria, agreed before testing. Agree two things separately with the customer before the test: the model accuracy required against the reference method, and the alarm or action threshold applied to the measured value.

premiseChecks.detail: Start with the simplest method that could meet the need and assess each method on its own; combine only if one is shown to be insufficient. A gain from combining is a hypothesis to test for this material.

premiseChecks.label: Probe geometry: transmission for an opaque medium
premiseChecks.detail: The medium is described as turbid, opaque or scattering. A transmission path saturates when light cannot penetrate the sample; ATR or reflection is used at high optical density.
